subject: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)
body:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

Hi all —

We’re close to landing the export flow for Usage Insights (cost drivers by route/model). Before we turn this on for beta, I’d like a quick cross-functional review on:

1) Audit logging fields for export create + download
2) RBAC/tenant isolation enforcement for the export APIs

Current implementation plan (high level):
- POST /usage-insights/exports creates an async job (CSV + JSON), returns export_job_id.
- GET /usage-insights/exports/{id} returns status + download URL when ready.
- GET /usage-insights/exports/{id}/download streams the file (no direct object store access).

Open questions where I’d like security/compliance guidance:
- Do we need to audit both “create export job” and “download export” as separate events? (My assumption: yes.)
- Required fields: should we log filters exactly as requested (route/model, region/env, time range), or a normalized/hash form for high-cardinality fields?
- How strict do we want RBAC on download vs create (e.g., user loses access after job created)? We currently re-check at download time.

Attaching the draft audit event spec we’re working against + the API contract addendum.

Attachments:
- usage-report-export-audit-events.json (draft)
- usage-insights-analytics-api-contract.json (draft)

If you can reply async with required changes, great. Otherwise I can grab 20 min tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan

—
Logan Wright
Engineering Manager, Telemetry & Analytics Platform
Redwood Inference


From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:06 AM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

+1 audit both create + download.

From an audit/compliance evidence perspective, we generally want a trail that can answer:
- who initiated the export
- what data scope it covered (tenant/project + filters)
- who actually retrieved it
- when/where (time + IP) it was retrieved

Recommendations (assuming we’re sticking to “bounded report” constraints):

Events:
A) usage_insights.export_job_created
B) usage_insights.export_downloaded
C) usage_insights.export_job_failed (optional but helpful)

Required fields (for A and B):
- actor_user_id, actor_email (if available), actor_role (org role)
- org_id, project_id (and deployment_mode if it affects dataset)
- export_job_id
- time_range_start, time_range_end
- requested_dimensions: route/model
- filters: region, environment, model (if pinned), route (if pinned)
- row_count, byte_count (for B, and for A once known)
- request_id / trace_id
- source_ip, user_agent (for B; for A if available)

On the “filters exactly vs hash”: My preference is to log the normalized filter string(s) *as submitted after validation*, but do NOT log raw route strings if they can contain customer data. If route identifiers can be customer-supplied, we should treat them as potentially sensitive.

So: log “route_filter_present=true” and route_count, and (optionally) log a truncated / normalized version if it meets the route naming requirements. But if route can be arbitrary, then hash is safer.

Question for you/Thomas: are we enforcing route normalization/allowed charset before it reaches this?

- Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
Security Engineering (Audit Logging & Governance)
Redwood Inference


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

A few RBAC/abuse-case questions:

1) When the export job runs async, what principal reads the underlying aggregates? Is it a service account with broad access? If so, we need to ensure the job is “scoped” to the creator’s org/project, and that we store that scope in the job record.

2) Can someone guess an export_job_id and download a file across projects? (Sounds like no since you’re doing GET /download via the API, but confirming.)

3) If a user is removed from a project between create and download, should download be blocked? (I’d expect yes; you mentioned re-checking.)

4) Are we allowing exports across multiple projects at once? That gets messy quickly from a governance standpoint.

Also please confirm we’re not issuing a long-lived pre-signed S3/GCS URL. Those are hard to revoke and tend to show up in customer security reviews.

- Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:27 AM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

Jumping in on RBAC mechanics.

Answers based on the current backend pattern (same as other console exports):

1) Async job principal: the worker runs as a service principal but the job payload includes immutable scope fields: org_id + project_id + environment + region (if applicable). The worker queries only with those params.

Important: we should *also* store creator_user_id and a snapshot of creator membership at create time (e.g., org_role + project_role) for investigation purposes, but enforcement should be real-time at API boundaries.

2) Guessing export_job_id: we use opaque IDs (not incremental) and we enforce org_id/project_id match in every handler. Additionally, the download endpoint checks the caller has access to the stored job scope.

3) Removal between create and download: yes, download should be blocked. This is consistent with our other artifact downloads and is what customers expect.

4) Multi-project exports: we should not allow for initial GA. It complicates tenancy and audit trails. Single project per export job is the cleanest.

Re: pre-signed URLs: agree. Better is API-streamed download behind auth + RBAC. If we ever need a pre-signed URL for perf reasons, it should be short-lived (minutes) and still gated behind an authenticated “mint URL” call.

Kaitlyn

—
Kaitlyn Nguyen
Backend Engineer, Tenant Isolation & RBAC
Redwood Inference


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 12:18 PM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

Adding product/security review notes:

- We should be explicit in the audit event schema that the export contains “usage and cost analytics” (not raw prompts/completions). That matters for how customers classify it.

- Filters captured in audit logs: I agree with Kevin — log validated/normalized filters, but avoid recording untrusted raw route strings if they can contain PII. From a compliance standpoint, logging customer-provided values into our internal audit log can create a second sensitive data store.

- Please include:
  - retention policy for export files (how long downloadable artifacts exist)
  - retention policy for audit log events (how long audit record exists)

- We should add an explicit audit field for export format(s): csv/json. Some customers ask.

- One more: consider adding “export_reason” as an optional string. Not required, but it’s useful for enterprise customers (incident review, FinOps, etc.). If we add it, it should be optional and not required for the flow.

Thanks,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & RBAC Product Review
Redwood Inference


From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:02 PM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

This is super helpful. Summarizing proposed decisions + action items so we can unblock ENG-8425/8428 + PR-15492.

Decisions:
1) Audit events: log both create + download as separate events.
   - A) usage_insights.export_job_created
   - B) usage_insights.export_downloaded
   - C) usage_insights.export_job_failed (we’ll include; low effort, good for investigations)

2) Download path: no direct object store URLs for GA; API-streamed download behind auth.

3) RBAC: enforce at both create and download.
   - Export job stores immutable scope (org_id/project_id/env/region)
   - On download, re-check caller membership/permissions against stored scope.

4) Multi-project exports: not in GA (single project per export).

Open items / changes we’ll make:
- Route filter logging: we will NOT log raw route strings in audit logs. We’ll log:
  - route_filter_present (true/false)
  - route_filter_count (int)
  - route_filter_hashes (optional; SHA-256 of normalized values) — Kevin, confirm if you want hashes or just presence/count for GA.

- Add audit fields:
  - export_formats (csv/json)
  - dataset_type = "usage_cost_analytics"
  - row_count + byte_count (once known)
  - creator_user_id + creator_role snapshot (for investigations only)

- Retention:
  - Export files: 7 days downloadable (current proposal)
  - Audit events: align with central audit log retention (currently 1 year) — Naomi/Kevin, please confirm.

Allison: any concerns from an observability standpoint about adding these audit events volume-wise?

If no objections by EOD tomorrow, we’ll proceed with these defaults and document in the audit event spec.

Logan


From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 4:07 PM
Subject: Re: Export audit + RBAC review (Usage Insights)

+1 to the summary/decisions.

Two product notes:
- Please keep “export_reason” out of GA unless it’s truly optional with no UI requirement. We can add later once we see enterprise demand.
- For route filter logging, I’m comfortable with presence/count only for GA. If a customer needs exact route values in the audit log, that’s going to be a bigger discussion anyway (and probably not desirable).

Thanks everyone — this is one of the top items coming up in the beta security reviews.

Paula

—
Paula Mendes
Product Manager, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
